subtopics.title: The Balanced Equation Is a Mole Recipe

questions.question: The coefficients of a balanced chemical equation give the ratio of:
options: Masses of the substances in grams
Volumes of the substances in all states
Moles of the substances
Densities of the substances

questions.question: The three legs of every stoichiometric journey, in order, are:
options: Mass to moles, mole ratio across the equation, moles back to the wanted unit
Balance, weigh, filter
Mole ratio, mass to moles, moles to mass
Grams across the equation, then convert to moles

questions.question: Why may a mass in grams never cross the equation directly?
options: Because grams are not an SI unit
Because the equation might be exothermic
Because masses are usually too large
Because a mole of each substance weighs a different amount, so the coefficient ratio is a mole ratio only

subtopics.title: The Prediction — 50 Grams In, How Much Out

questions.question: The molar mass of CaCO₃ (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16) is:
options: 68 g/mol
100 g/mol
84 g/mol
116 g/mol

questions.question: 50 g of CaCO₃ converted to moles gives:
options: 2 mol
5 mol
0,5 mol
0,2 mol

questions.question: Using the 1 : 1 ratio and M(CaO) = 56 g/mol, the theoretical yield of CaO from 0,5 mol CaCO₃ is:
The conservation-of-mass check works here because 28 g CaO plus 22 g CO₂:
options: Rounds to 56 g, the molar mass of CaO
Is less than the 50 g of reactant, proving gas escaped
Shows the reaction created 6 g of new matter
Equals the 50 g of CaCO₃ that decomposed — atoms are conserved

questions.question: Percentage yield is calculated as:
options: Theoretical yield divided by actual yield, times 100
Actual yield divided by theoretical yield, times 100
Actual yield minus theoretical yield
Theoretical yield times actual yield, divided by 100

questions.question: An actual yield of 25,2 g against a theoretical 28 g gives a percentage yield of:
Which is a genuine physical reason for a yield below 100%?
options: Incomplete reaction and product lost during transfers
The theoretical yield was calculated too accurately
Moles were used instead of grams
The balanced equation had coefficients of one

questions.question: A learner reports a yield of 108%. The correct conclusion is:
options: The reaction overachieved its ratio
The theoretical yield formula must be wrong
Extra atoms were created by the heat
Something is wrong — the product is likely wet or contaminated, since atoms cannot deliver more than the ceiling

subtopics.title: The Full Method, the Classic Traps, and Where This Leads

questions.question: The FIRST step of every stoichiometry problem is:
options: Convert the given mass to moles
Calculate the percentage yield
Write and balance the chemical equation
Find the molar mass of the product

questions.question: For CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂, the mole ratio is 1 : 1 but the mass ratio of carbonate to oxide is:
options: 100 : 56 — the same count of moles weighs different amounts
1 : 1, masses always follow coefficients
56 : 100 — the product is always heavier
44 : 56 — set by the escaping gas

questions.question: A learner computes yield as 28 ÷ 25,2 × 100 = 111%. The error is:
options: Using grams instead of moles
The fraction is inverted — actual belongs on top, and the impossible answer over 100% is the giveaway
Forgetting to multiply by 100
Using the wrong molar mass for CaO

questions.question: Exam phrases like 'maximum mass' or 'at most' signal that the question wants:
options: The actual yield from the laboratory
The percentage yield
The mass of the leftover reactant
The theoretical yield — the ceiling the atoms allow

subtopics.title: A Recipe Promises, in Its Own Units

questions.question: The bakery comparison says a balanced equation promises 'one batch gives one tray'. The chemical units of that promise are:
options: Grams to grams
Litres to litres
Moles to moles
Atoms to grams

questions.question: One mole of CaCO₃ weighs 100 g while one mole of CaO weighs 56 g. This shows that:
options: The same mole count of different substances has different masses
The equation is unbalanced
Half the calcium disappears
CaO contains more atoms per mole

questions.question: The 'two doors' of the stoichiometric journey are:
options: Balancing and weighing
Heating and cooling
Mixing and filtering
Grams to moles on the way in; moles to grams on the way out — each using that substance's own molar mass

subtopics.title: Fifty Grams of Chalk Through the Bakery

questions.question: 50 g of CaCO₃ at 100 g per mole is:
options: Two moles
Half a mole
Five moles
One fifth of a mole

questions.question: The 'other 22 grams' of the original 50 g:
options: Were destroyed by the heat
Stayed in the crucible as calcium
Left as 0,5 mol of carbon dioxide gas — the atoms changed address, not existence
Turned into energy

questions.question: In a decomposition, the product masses must add up to the reactant mass. If they refuse to:
options: The mistake is in your arithmetic, not in the atoms
The law of conservation of mass has an exception
Gas products should be left out of the total
The reaction must have been exothermic

questions.question: The word 'most' in 'the oven can deliver at most 28 grams' identifies 28 g as:
options: The actual yield
The percentage yield
The mass of escaped gas
The theoretical yield — a ceiling set by the atoms

questions.question: In the bakery picture, percentage yield is:
options: The oven temperature as a percentage
The shelf count divided by the recipe's promise, times 100
The promise divided by the shelf count, times 100
The number of trays baked per day

questions.question: Collecting 25,2 g against a promised 28 g is a yield of 90%, which for a school laboratory is:
options: Impossible — school yields are always below 50%
A sign the equation was unbalanced
Genuinely good — some shortfall is normal and expected
A failure that must be repeated

questions.question: Which pairing of bakery picture to chemical cause is correct?
options: Rolls stuck to the pan — product left behind on the crucible and spatula
Rolls stuck to the pan — a side reaction
An unfinished bake — product lost in transfer
Dough pinched before baking — incomplete heating

questions.question: A yield over 100% means 'a contaminated tray, never a generous oven' — in chemical terms:
options: The reaction produced bonus product
The theoretical yield was set too low
The percentage sign was forgotten
The weighed product contains extra mass such as moisture or unreacted material
